title: Population Density Globe with Particle Effects
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D population density globe visualization using Three.js. Follow these specifications exactly:

## Scene Setup
- Initialize a Three.js scene with a dark navy background (0x0a0a2e).
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.5) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 1.0) at position (5, 5, 5).
- Implement OrbitControls for camera rotation, with auto-rotate enabled at speed 0.5.

## Globe
- Create a sphere (radius 1.5, 64 segments) with a semi-transparent blue wireframe material (0x2244aa, opacity 0.3, wireframe true) to represent Earth.
- Add the sphere to the scene as the main globe object.

## 3D Asset - Corset Model
- Load the 'Corset.glb' model using GLTFLoader. This model serves as a decorative data-station marker placed on the globe surface.
- Scale the loaded model to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3).
- Position it at (1.5, 0, 0) on the globe surface.
- Name the loaded model's scene 'corsetMarker'.
- The model should rotate slowly on its Y-axis (0.01 rad/frame).

## Population Density Particles
- Create a particle system using THREE.Points with THREE.BufferGeometry.
- Generate exactly 2000 particles distributed on the globe surface using spherical coordinates.
- Particles should have varying sizes (1-4) and colors based on simulated density:
  - High density (red, 0xff3333): 30% of particles, clustered in specific regions
  - Medium density (yellow, 0xffaa33): 40% of particles
  - Low density (green, 0x33ff66): 30% of particles
- Store particle count in state. Particles should gently pulse (scale oscillation using sin(time)).

## HUD / UI Elements
- Add a title div at top-center: 'Population Density Globe' in white, font-size 24px, id='title'.
- Add a stats panel (id='statsPanel') at top-right showing: 'Particles: 2000' and 'Auto-Rotate: ON'.
- Add three DOM buttons at bottom-center:
  1. id='btnToggleRotate' - text 'Toggle Rotation' - toggles auto-rotate on/off
  2. id='btnToggleParticles' - text 'Toggle Particles' - shows/hides the particle system
  3. id='btnResetView' - text 'Reset View' - resets camera to initial position (0, 2, 5)

## Keyboard Interactions
- Press 'P' key: Toggle particle visibility (same as btnToggleParticles)
- Press 'R' key: Reset camera view (same as btnResetView)
- Press 'Space' key: Toggle auto-rotation (same as btnToggleRotate)

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with the following fields, updated every frame:
  - particleCount: number (2000)
  - particlesVisible: boolean (true initially)
  - autoRotate: boolean (true initially)
  - cameraX: number (camera.position.x)
  - cameraY: number (camera.position.y)
  - cameraZ: number (camera.position.z)
  - globeExists: boolean (true if globe mesh exists in scene)
  - corsetLoaded: boolean (true once Corset.glb is loaded)
  - corsetRotationY: number (current Y rotation of corset model)
  - frameCount: number (incremented each animation frame)

## Animation Loop
- Animate particles pulsing, corset rotation, and globe auto-rotation.
- Update __3D_STATE__ every frame.
- Increment frameCount each frame starting from 0.
physics_constraints: Particles must remain on or near the globe surface (distance from origin ~1.5 +/- 0.3). Camera position values must never be NaN. Auto-rotate should smoothly orbit the camera around the Y-axis.
